away.name: Cam Talbot
away.news: Jet Greaves has struggled this season, resulting in Talbot playing more in recent weeks. The 39-year-old Talbot is coming off a solid performance in Saturday's 4-3 win over the Toronto Maple Leafs, saving 23 of 26 shots (.885 SV%). In his last eight games (6-2-0), Talbot has an impressive 2.34 GAA and .921 SV%. That said, the Blue Jackets enter Monday's matchup as +172 road underdogs against the New Jersey Devils, who have lost two straight (0-2-0).

home.name: Connor Hellebuyck
home.news: Hellebuyck has been solid since joining the New Jersey Devils, but has strung together several poor outings, most notably Saturday's 9-6 loss to the St. Louis Blues, where he allowed four goals on six shots (.333 SV%). In his last three appearances, Hellebuyck has 5.19 GAA and .863 SV%. That said, he still sports a 7-1-0 record. He should be a solid option on Monday, with the Devils entering action as -191 home favourites against the Columbus Blue Jackets, who have the worst offensive output in the Eastern Conference (2.57 GF/GP).

home.name: Jakub Dobes
home.news: After a breakout 2025-26 season that continued with an impressive postseason run, Dobes has struggled early in 2026-27. As a result, the Canadiens have often turned to Jacob Fowler, but Dobes has strung together a couple of solid outings. The 25-year-old Czech goalie is coming off his best performance of the season, saving 26 of 27 shots (.963 SV%) in a 2-1 overtime win over the Carolina Hurricanes. The Canadiens enter Monday's action as -149 home favourites against a low-scoring Los Angeles Kings team that has lost 14 of their first 21 games (7-12-2).

away.name: Devin Cooley
away.news: Cooley was playing the best hockey of his NHL career before suffering a lower-body injury that sidelined him for over a week in late October. That said, he has not been able to find the same success since returning. The 29-year-old Cooley struggled in his most recent game, allowing five goals on 33 shots (.848 SV%) in a 6-1 loss to the Anaheim Ducks. Cooley has lost three of his past four games (1-3-0), posting a 3.29 GAA and .890 SV%. The Flames enter Monday's game as sizeable +217 road underdogs against a rolling Ottawa Senators team that has points in eight straight games (6-0-2).

home.name: Linus Ullmark
home.news: Ullmark missed nearly three weeks with a lower-body injury, but hasn't missed a step since returning, continuing a tremendous start to the 2026-27 season. The 33-year-old Swedish goalie was solid in his most recent outing, saving 19 of 21 shots (.905 SV%) in a 4-2 win over the Los Angeles Kings. Ullmark has allowed two or fewer goals in all but one of 12 games this season (11-1-0). The Senators enter Monday's contest as significant -247 home favourites against a Calgary Flames team that is 3-1-1 in their past five games.

away.name: Anthony Stolarz
away.news: When the Maple Leafs signed Bobrovsky to a three-year, $7 million AAV contract ($21M total) in the offseason, the hope was that he could solidify their crease and return the team to the postseason. That said, Bobrovsky has been less than stellar, increasing Stolarz's workload, who will return to the crease for the fifth time in six games. The 32-year-old Stolarz has unquestionably been more reliable than Bobrovsky, but even so, the Maple Leafs remain locked in an ugly nine-game losing streak (0-8-1). The Maple Leafs enter Monday's game as +143 road underdogs against the New York Islanders, who have points in seven straight games (4-0-3).

away.name: Sebastian Cossa
away.news: Karel Vejmelka was expected to lead Utah between the pipes this season, but early-season struggles have opened a door for rookie Sebastian Cossa in recent outings. The 24-year-old Cossa has been inconsistent this season, but has shown encouraging signs, including his past two games (2-0-0), where he has saved 59 of 62 shots (.952 SV%). The Mammoth enter Monday's game as -101 road underdogs against a Winnipeg Jets team that is 7-1-1 in their past nine games.

home.name: Stuart Skinner
home.news: Skinner has had an inconsistent first season with Winnipeg, but has done enough on most nights to give his team a fighting chance. In his most recent game, Skinner allowed four goals on 33 shots (.879 SV%), which was enough to help the Jets secure a point in a 5-4 shootout loss to the Vegas Golden Knights. The 28-year-old goalie has a 4-1-1 record in his last seven appearances with a 3.27 GAA and .876 SV%. The Jets enter Monday's game as slight +100 home underdogs against a Utah Mammoth team coming off a 3-2 win over the Anaheim Ducks.

away.name: Filip Gustavsson
away.news: Gustavsson was recalled from Iowa on Monday after a one-game conditioning stint, in which he recorded a win while saving 29 of 32 shots (.906 SV%), marking his first game since his off-season hip surgery. The 27-year-old Gustavsson is entering the first year of a five-year, $38 million contract extension ($6.8 million AAV) and is poised to compete for playing time with counterpart Jesper Wallstedt, who has become Minnesota's de facto starting goalie and one of the NHL's top goalies this season. Minnesota enters Monday's matchup as -170 road favourites against the San Jose Sharks, who are 4-1-1 in their past six games.

home.name: Yaroslav Askarov
home.news: Askarov had a rough performance in his most recent outing, allowing 24 of shots (.857 SV%) in a 5-2 loss to the Calgary Flames. The 24-year-old goalie has been inconsistent this season, allowing four or more goals in seven of 16 games (6-9-1). The Sharks enter Monday's contest as +153 home underdogs against a Minnesota Wild team that is without Quinn Hughes (upper body) and is coming off a 4-3 loss to the Vancouver Canucks.
